newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index falls at noon on clampdown talk.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index falls at noon on clampdown talk.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended Tuesday morning substantially lower with trading dominated by talk of possible strong government measures to cool down the surging markets, analysts said.
The foreign currency B index lost 3.88 points or 2.11 percent to 179.62 on turnover of HK$55.6 million.
"Rumours of a looming crackdown are simmering," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
The A share index ended the morning 7.83 points or 1.43 percent lower at 538.18, after spiking to an historical high of 546.74 on Monday.
Traders said the government was rumoured to be planning to extend the settlement period for transactions to three days to reduce market volatility.
This compares with the current settlement period of one day for A shares and immediate settlement for B shares, analysts said.
"This could dry up market liquidity," the J&A analyst said.
A Hong Kong newspaper on Tuesday said Chinese authorities could "no longer tolerate the crazy market gains," and would likely announce clampdown measures in the short term.
"Apart from extending the settlement period, the government is also seen as planning to rein in several brokerages," an analyst at a major investment bank said.
"Trading volume on the B share market is small, indicating a wait-and-see sentiment for the afternoon," an analyst at Central-South Securities said.
Shenzhen Textile Holdings Co Ltd was the sharpest loser in the B share market, shedding HK$0.22 or 5.18 percent to HK$4.03.
Shenzhen Tellus Machinery & Electronics Co Ltd, was the worst performer on the A share market, losing 0.65 yuan or 6.20 percent to 9.84 yuan.
